subject: english-language
source_note: Topic structure follows the Eduqas/WJEC GCSE English Language specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

topics.name: Prose Comprehension
topics.blurb: Locating and interpreting explicit and implicit meaning

topics.name: Analysing Literary Language
topics.blurb: How writers use language and structure for effect

topics.name: Evaluating Texts
topics.blurb: Critical, evaluative response to a writer's methods

topics.name: Synthesis of Two Texts
topics.blurb: Drawing together ideas across two sources

topics.name: Comparing Writers' Viewpoints
topics.blurb: Comparing perspectives and methods across eras

topics.name: Transactional Writing
topics.blurb: Letters, articles, reports, reviews and speeches

topics.name: Persuasive Writing
topics.blurb: Rhetoric and argument for a clear purpose

topics.name: Presentation Skills
topics.blurb: Planning and delivering a spoken presentation

topics.name: Spoken Standard English
topics.blurb: Responding to questions in formal register

topics.name: Vocabulary & Register
topics.blurb: Precise, ambitious word choice for context

connections.why: You must understand a text before analysing how it works
Evaluation builds on analysis to judge a writer's success
Studying writers' techniques models choices for your own prose
Both creative tasks share imagery, structure and craft
Synthesis combines information accurately retrieved from texts
Comparison extends synthesis into evaluating viewpoints
Reading persuasive non-fiction reveals rhetorical techniques to reuse
Transactional tasks usually require persuasion for audience and purpose
Register and word choice must suit the reader and form
Technical accuracy is assessed across all writing (SPaG 20%)
Accurate grammar and punctuation underpin every written response
The same analytical toolkit serves literary and non-fiction reading
A strong presentation depends on confident Standard English
Rhetorical technique transfers from the page to the spoken task
